caroline_docs: FYI opened a tiny PR that tries to clarify what happens when a tenant triggers a short surge (burst) and we fall back to lower-tier capacity. I added an SDK example for exponential backoff + a short YAML snippet for autoscale cooldown but want eyes on wording for isolation guarantees.
ben_engineering: thanks — link?
caroline_docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842 (will paste snippets here)
dave_pm: high level question: do we want the doc to promise no request loss or just best-effort retry when fallback occurs? Legal asked for precise language.
elena_sre: we can't promise zero loss, but we do guarantee requests are routed to a compatible variant; if variant is rate-limited those requests may get 429 and clients should retry. Suggest wording: "best-effort routing with transparent fallbacks; clients should implement backoff."
sam_writer: ok I'll rephrase to that. Also we should call out the isolation footnote — e.g., when a tenant is preempted from Dedicated reserved pool due to shard reclamation, cached prefix state might be lost and latency/spike behavior differs.
caroline_docs: here's the SDK snippet I added — want to make sure it's accurate:

```python
# SDK example: simple exponential backoff for fallback 429s
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)

def call_with_backoff(prompt, max_retries=5):
    backoff = 0.5
    for i in range(max_retries):
        resp = client.generate(prompt)
        if resp.status_code == 200:
            return resp
        if resp.status_code == 429:
            time.sleep(backoff)
            backoff *= 2
            continue
        raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected {resp.status_code}")
    raise RuntimeError("failed after retries")
```

ben_engineering: minor nit: our client returns exceptions rather than status_code sometimes. Suggest using client.generate(..., raise_for_status=False) in example or catching RateLimitError.
caroline_docs: good point — I'll change to catch RateLimitError.
dave_pm: YAML snippet where? I see a cooldown example but not the labeled field name. We use "cooldown_seconds" in the autoscaler model right?
elena_sre: yes, cooldown_seconds on the scalePolicy; default 120. Maybe call out recommended values for bursty workloads (60-300).
sam_writer: added short note: "If you expect short spikes, set cooldown_seconds to a lower value and combine with prefix caching to reduce cold-start token cost."
caroline_docs: copying the YAML I added:

```yaml
# recommended scalePolicy for tenant surge handling
scalePolicy:
  type: predictive
  cooldown_seconds: 90  # lower for short spikes
  burst_capacity: 2     # allow short extra nodes for a tenant
  preemption_policy: fallthrough  # falls back to compatible variant
```

dave_pm: tiny wording request: replace "fallthrough" with "fallback" to match other docs.
caroline_docs: done. updated PR.
ben_engineering: also put an inline link to the runtime guarantees doc that explains "compatible variant" behavior.
caroline_docs: added link and a one-line pointer to "what changes during fallback" section.
deploy-bot: PR #842 merged to main by caroline_docs
caroline_docs: thanks all! I'll follow up with a short changelog entry for release notes. :sparkles:
